speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. I understand you have a history of gait and limb ataxia; could you describe exactly how your walking has been affected and when these symptoms first appeared?

speaker: Patient
text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that description. Is the clumsiness on your right side constant, or does it only happen when you try to walk? Have you noticed any changes in your sense of touch, like numbness or tingling, in your limbs or face?

speaker: Patient
text: I have Crohn disease and it has been difficult to control. I have been taking natalizumab for about a year.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: PML (Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy) secondary to natalizumab therapy in the setting of Crohn's disease.

I am concerned about your recent neurologic symptoms combined with natalizumab use; this combination carries a significant risk for PML. Have you noticed any new visual changes, such as blind spots or double vision, or any recent fever? REQUEST TEST: MRI Brain with contrast. REQUEST IMAGES.
